findings.question: cmux performance benchmarks: sessions per instance, memory usage per session, client connection limits, network bandwidth per client
findings.answer: NO QUANTITATIVE BENCHMARKS AVAILABLE. cmux (manaflow-ai/cmux) launched Feb 2026, post-training cutoff. Architectural analysis suggests cmux is NOT comparable to traditional multiplexers (tmux/screen): it's a macOS GUI application (Swift + Ghostty) with vertical tabs, NOT a client-server architecture. Traditional metrics (sessions per instance, client connections) do not apply - cmux is single-user, single-machine. Based on architecture findings: (1) Each tab is a separate Ghostty instance with Unix socket IPC, (2) No documented client/server protocol exists, (3) ~5k lines codebase suggests lightweight design. Performance would be limited by: macOS memory/process limits, Ghostty's rendering overhead per tab, Swift UI framework constraints. Comparison baseline: tmux supports 100+ sessions per instance with ~10-50MB base memory + 2-5MB per session; Ghostty uses GPU rendering (Metal on macOS) which is memory-intensive but fast. CONCLUSION: Specific cmux benchmarks do NOT exist in accessible sources. Would require: (1) GitHub issue search for user-reported performance data, (2) cmux repository benchmark suite analysis, (3) Manual testing with htop/Activity Monitor.
